newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus names commercial banker central bank chief.
newsitem.headline: Belarus names commercial banker central bank chief.

text.p: Belarus on Thursday put a leading commercial banker, Gennady Aleinikov, in charge of its central bank after his predecessor was arrested on corruption charges.

Aleinikov, 50, president of one of the former Soviet republic's top five commercial banks, was taking over from Tamara Vinnikova who is in custody, an official in President Alexander Lukashenko's administration told Reuters.

State television said on Wednesday that Vinnikova's deputy, Nikolai Korbut, was carrying out her duties after she was sacked for causing what state radio called "damage to the state of major proportions".
Aleinikov has always worked in the banking sector and from 1989 to 1992 was deputy head of the former Soviet foreign economic bank in the republic of 10 million.
He will report directly to Lukashenko and was one of two replacements the president had said last week he was considering for Vinnikova's post in the event she was dismissed.

The administration official said a survey among commercial bankers for their preferred candidate put Aleinikov in first place. Vinnikova, appointed last February, was placed behind both the possible replacements.
Aleinikov's Belvneshekonombank (Belarussian Foreign Economic Bank) was the first to introduce credit cards and cash machines in the capital Minsk and he is popular in the banking sector.
But one banker who asked not to be named said he feared Aleinikov could find his new position threatened by the presidential administration.
The charges against Vinnikova are reported to be connected to her activities before she joined the central bank.
She once headed Belarusbank, which merged with the state savings bank in 1995 to create the country's biggest bank.
On Wednesday, Russia's Interfax news agency quoted an unnamed source at the prosecutor's office as saying Vinnikova was arrested because of "abuse of her position and financial machinations".
The alleged irregularities were uncovered during checks of financial activities at Belarusbank instigated by Lukashenko himself, Interfax quoted the source as saying.
Vinnikova had initially been an unquestioning supporter of Lukashenko's reluctant approach to market reforms, but over time objected to many of his policies.
